description:
We are a team of curious storytellers fascinated by space and the traces humans leave beyond Earth.  

We chose forgotten equipment in space because every object has a journey, but not every journey gets told. Through storytelling, we bring these forgotten objects back into the spotlight and imagine the incredible stories they could share.  

Cosmic Footprint represents the footprints humanity leaves among the stars. Small Things. Big Stories.
summary:
Our team, Orbit Trove developed an interactive, 3D web-based storytelling platform that shows the Mars exploration journeys of NASA’s three rovers: Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity. Guided by an animated robot named NEO, users embark on a chapter-by-chapter journey across the Martian landscape, experiencing key milestones from Pathfinder’s airbag-cushioned bounce to Spirit’s geological search in Gusev Crater and Opportunity last message to Earth on June 10, 2018 

The Website is an interactive 3D web experience structured into three narrative chapters for each rover Ch 1 Sojourner/Pathfinder, Ch 2: Spirit, and Ch 3: Opportunity. Users navigate through mission stops like landing sequences, crater explorations, and final resting sites on a 3D Martian globe and terrain map. In the journey NEO explains the science, and historical context behind every milestone, while showing us Martian topography such as Gusev Crater, Perseverance Valley with rover models, the craters, hills, scattered boulders.

Our game provides a clean user interface provided with interactive playback controls, allowing users to Pause/Resume the mission replay, toggle Sound, open Tour controls to jump between stops, or click Back to globe to switch between rover missions.

And finally, our goal is to inspire students, space enthusiasts, and excited learners to explore planetary science, demonstrating how interactive web technologies can make real-world space explorations fun and engaging.
details:
# Project Description

**Mars Explore** is an interactive 3D website created for NASA Space Apps’ *Abandoned but Not Forgotten* challenge. It follows Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity, three missions whose equipment remains on Mars. Visitors can take a guided expedition with Neo, a fictional robot narrator, or explore the landing sites on an interactive globe. **Rover Rush**, a companion desktop game, invites them to revisit the same missions through play.

## The guided expedition

Neo tells the story of each mission through animated rover journeys, close-up views of scientific clues, and short explanations delivered beside the scene. As a rover approaches a point of interest, the camera frames the feature and Neo explains what the visitor is seeing. Visitors can pause, revisit a stop, or open an optional inspection. On-screen dialogue makes the tour usable with the sound off.

In Ares Vallis, visitors can inspect rounded pebbles and discover why their shape suggested that water once flowed there. Separate illustrations show Pathfinder’s observations of magnetic airborne dust and early morning clouds of water ice. At Columbia Hills, the tour highlights rocks that Spirit found to have been altered by water. At Eagle Crater, a close-up reveals the tiny spheres nicknamed “blueberries” that Opportunity studied while investigating the region’s wet past. The website draws on NASA mission records and labels reconstructed scenes and routes as schematic. Reported measurements, such as Opportunity’s 45.16-kilometer lifetime odometer, appear separately from the distances illustrated in the animations.

The expedition also shows how each mission ended. Sojourner relayed its observations through the Pathfinder lander, and Earth stopped hearing from the rover after Pathfinder’s final transmission. Spirit became stuck in soft soil before the winter that preceded its final contact. Opportunity fell silent after a planet-wide dust storm reduced the sunlight reaching its solar panels in Perseverance Valley. Each ending returns to the evidence the rover sent home and what scientists learned from it.

## Rover Rush

Rover Rush is a keyboard-controlled, side-scrolling platformer for desktop browsers. Its three courses take inspiration from Ares Vallis, Gusev Crater, and Meridiani Planum. Players learn each rover’s controls, collect optional mission facts called Memory Fragments, and answer questions at the end of each course. The courses compress real distances for play. Sojourner’s Airbag Bounce, for example, adapts Pathfinder’s real landing system into an arcade ability.

## Development and tools

We built Mars Explore with **HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, Three.js, and JSON**. Three.js renders the globe, rover models, and Neo’s procedural character animation. The website uses **glTF/GLB** model assets and **OrbitControls** for globe navigation. HTML overlays display dialogue, controls, and source links. A cue-based tour coordinates camera movement, on-screen dialogue, Neo’s gestures, and scene changes. We designed Neo’s voice with **ElevenLabs Voice Design** and used ElevenLabs text-to-speech to generate narration.

Rover Rush uses **Phaser 3**, JavaScript, JSON level configurations, sprite sheets for rover animations, and procedural pixel art for terrain and effects. Shared game logic handles input and progression, while each mission’s data defines its course and educational content. We used **Claude Code** for implementation and debugging, **OpenAI Codex** for requirements and script development, **GitHub** for project files, and **Vercel** to host Rover Rush. We developed on a **Windows laptop** using **PowerShell** and tested the website in various browsers.

We want younger audiences and visitors new to Mars exploration to leave with a story they can retell. A visitor might remember Opportunity’s blueberries first, then be able to explain how those spheres helped scientists build a case for ancient water. The project gives visitors a way to trace that reasoning from the landscape to the evidence and see why the missions’ observations still matter.

# Mars Explore and Rover Rush — Submission Resource Inventory

For the Space Apps form, enter each resource name in **Link Text** and its complete address in **URL**. Use the non-NASA table for **Space Agency Partner & Other Data** and the NASA table for **NASA Data**.

This inventory reflects the Mars Explore source on the repository's main branch, the published Rover Rush build at https://game.rovemars.study/, and the project handoff. The Rover Rush source folder and its build scripts were not inspected directly. The final code may contain additional resources.

## Space Agency Partner & Other Data

| Link Text | URL | Project use |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Three.js | https://threejs.org/ | Mars Explore 3D rendering, including the OrbitControls (globe rotation, zoom, and pan) and GLTFLoader (Mars and rover GLB models) add-ons. The site imports 0.180.0. |

| GSAP | https://gsap.com/ | Mars Explore camera-flight animation. The site imports 3.13.0. |

| Phaser 3 | https://github.com/phaserjs/phaser/tree/v3.60.0 | Rover Rush 2D game framework. The game imports 3.60.0. |

| jsDelivr | https://www.jsdelivr.com/ | CDN for the Three.js, GSAP, and Phaser imports. |

| VT323 — Google Fonts | https://fonts.google.com/specimen/VT323 | Pixel-style interface font loaded by Rover Rush. Mars Explore uses the system font. |

| ElevenLabs Voice Design | https://elevenlabs.io/voice-design | Creation of Neo’s custom narrator voice. |

| ElevenLabs Text to Speech with Timing | https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert-with-timestamps | Narration generation and cue synchronization. |

| ElevenLabs Models (Multilingual v2) | https://elevenlabs.io/docs/models | Voice model used for Neo’s narration (`eleven_multilingual_v2`). |

| Claude Code | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview | Website and game implementation and debugging. |

| OpenAI Codex | https://openai.com/codex/ | Requirements, upgrade prompts, and script development. |

| Mars Explore source code (GitHub) | https://github.com/siva-shanm/mars_xplore | Mars Explore source code and deployment source. |

| Vercel | https://vercel.com/ | Hosting for Mars Explore (www.rovemars.study) and Rover Rush (game.rovemars.study). |

| Microsoft PowerShell | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/ | Windows terminal for local development and Claude Code. |

| Python | https://www.python.org/ | Local HTTP serving, narration generation, site packaging, and game asset processing. |

| Node.js | https://nodejs.org/ | Mars Explore unit tests (`tests/*.mjs`) and Rover Rush level building (`tools/build_levels.mjs`). |

| NumPy | https://numpy.org/ | Array processing in Rover Rush’s asset scripts. |

| Pillow | https://python-pillow.org/ | Image loading and processing in Rover Rush’s asset scripts. |

| SciPy | https://scipy.org/ | Image processing in Rover Rush’s asset scripts. |

| Playwright | https://playwright.dev/ | Mars Explore browser testing with Chromium, documented in the README. |

Other technologies include HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, JSON, WebGL, and glTF/GLB. The project was developed on a Windows laptop and tested in various browsers. No non-NASA space-agency dataset was identified in the materials inspected.

## NASA Data

| Link Text | URL | Project use |

| --- | --- | --- |

| NASA Mars Pathfinder | https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-pathfinder/ | Pathfinder and Sojourner mission history, landing, and observations. Also a Rover Rush fact source. |

| Mars Pathfinder Landing Ellipses | https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/mars-pathfinder-landing-ellipses/ | Pathfinder landing position reference. |

| NASA Spirit Mission | https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mer-spirit/ | Spirit’s site, journey, findings, and mission ending. Also a Rover Rush fact source. |

| Spirit’s Trip to the Hills | https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/spirits-trip-to-the-hills/ | Columbia Hills traverse context. |

| NASA Opportunity Mission | https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mer-opportunity/ | Opportunity’s route history, distance, and mission ending. Also a Rover Rush fact source. |

| Mars Exploration Rovers — Spirit and Opportunity | https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-exploration-rovers-spirit-and-opportunity/ | Shared mission context and science. |

| Mars Exploration Rovers Science Highlights | https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-exploration-rovers-spirit-and-opportunity/science-highlights/ | Science findings, including Opportunity’s evidence of ancient water. |

| NASA Mars Fact Sheet | https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html | Mars radius for globe scale. |

| Planet Mars, 3D Model | https://science.nasa.gov/resource/planet-mars-3d-model/ | Source of `Mars3dmodel.glb`, the Mars Explore globe model and textures. The file is byte-identical to NASA’s `24881_Mars_1_6792.glb`. |

| Spirit and Opportunity Rover 3D Model | https://science.nasa.gov/resource/spirit-and-opportunity-rover-3d-model/ | Source of `Spirit&Opportunity3dmodel.glb`, the Spirit and Opportunity rover model in Mars Explore. The file is byte-identical to NASA’s `24883_MER_static.glb`. |

| NASA’s Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven | https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/perseverance-mars-rover/2026/10/12/nasas-perseverance-sets-off-world-record-for-total-distance-driven/ | Rover Rush fact source for Sojourner’s distance driven (about 330 feet, or 100 meters). |
